label: digit 2 input at original positions 0-2
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is the digit 2 at one of the first three original positions (t = 0, 1, 2). It never fires on 2 at later original positions (t >= 3), on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (3 stray activations at t=5), and never on any other token. Magnitude depends on position and preceding token: about 0.72 of max at t=0, highest at t=1 (max reached after a leading i, about 0.9 after other tokens), and 0.64-0.9 at t=2. A repeated 2 (not first occurrence) still fires, at slightly lower strength (about 0.67-0.69).

issues: Core predicate holds. On the test split precision is 1.000, recall 0.99992, F1 0.99996 and mass recall 0.99999, with 0 false positives.

The only misses are 4 test activations, all on input 2 at step 5 in the copy phase, with relative activation 0.03-0.12 (about 0% of activation mass). All 4 have the same pattern: an L=3 sequence of the form 'X 2 z <DEL> X [2]'. This is a narrow tail with negligible mass. Strictly, it contradicts 'never fires on a 2 at t >= 3', but the explanation does mention the 3 copy-phase firings at t=5 on dev.

One magnitude claim is partly wrong. 'A repeated 2 still fires, a little weaker (about 0.67-0.69)' holds for a repeated 2 at t=2 (e.g. y [2:0.94] [2:0.67], 2 w [2:0.70]). But a 2 at t=1 right after a 2 at t=0 is NOT weaker: '[2:0.72] [2:0.91]' and 'i [2:1.00] [2:0.68]' show the weakening depends on position. This is a minor inaccuracy and does not affect the predicate.
The other magnitude claims check out against profile examples: max 1.0 at t=1 after first token i, t=0 about 0.72, t=2 from 0.64 to 0.9.
